title: MOSAIC: Towards a Universal Latent Space for Computational Pathology Foundation Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.33059v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Pathology foundation models (PFMs) differ substantially in architecture, pretraining objective, training data and representation dimensionality, yet it remains unclear whether they learn fundamentally different feature spaces or alternative coordinate systems of a shared underlying representation. We present MOSAIC, a systematic study of latent-space similarity, alignment and interoperability across $12$ patch-level and $6$ slide-level PFMs. We first quantify representational agreement using complementary similarity measures and analyze how architecture, pretraining objective, network depth and magnification influence latent geometry. We then evaluate multiple alignment strategies for mapping independently learned representations into a common latent space. The resulting representations are evaluated through cross-model agreement, retrieval, geometry preservation, and downstream multiple-instance learning across molecular and morpholog

translated_title: MOSAIC：迈向计算病理学基础模型的通用潜空间
translated_abstract: 病理学基础模型（PFMs）在架构、预训练目标、训练数据和表示维度上存在显著差异，然而它们究竟学习到了根本不同的特征空间，还是同一共享底层表示的不同坐标系，目前仍不清楚。我们提出了MOSAIC，这是一项针对12个patch级和6个slide级病理学基础模型的潜空间相似性、对齐性和互操作性的系统性研究。我们首先使用互补的相似性度量方法量化表示之间的一致性，并分析架构、预训练目标、网络深度和放大倍数如何影响潜空间几何结构。随后，我们评估了多种将独立学习的表示映射到共同潜空间的对齐策略。所得的表示通过跨模型一致性、检索、几何保持以及在分子和形态学终点上的下游多示例学习任务进行评估。
tldr: MOSAIC系统性地研究了12个patch级和6个slide级病理学基础模型的潜空间相似性与对齐性，发现这些模型可被映射到一个通用的共享潜空间，并在检索、几何保持和下游多示例学习任务中保持性能。
